author_and_execution: Codex; no DeepSeek/Claude; read-only public-source retrieval; no application or DMA executed

decision.candidate: HERO Matrix-Matrix Multiplication with Double Buffering Example Application
decision.relationship_to_arxiv1808_09751: New official PULP/same-author source adaptation, not reproduction of original SP benchmark. Neither operational-intensity sweep points nor unrelated kernels are spliced into phases.
decision.main_finding: A concrete double-buffer application exists, with two distinct input streams plus output. It has six scratchpad slots rather than the previous provisional four-slot template; source computes a fixed kernel, not an adjustable wait loop.
decision.no_performance_conclusion: No compute-cycle duration, shared-IOMMU interference result, DMA timing, FPGA validation, or new-rule benefit is accepted by source reading alone.

bounded_search.method: Exact title/author/official-site web search followed by unauthenticated GitHub repository, commit, recursive tree, selected raw-file and file-history GET requests. No third official repository inspected and no ecosystem clone.
queries: "Scalable and Efficient Virtual Memory Sharing" GitHub pulp
bounded_search.result_scope: No obtainable original SP C source or artifact link was identified in these searches and the two fixed current repository trees. This is not proof that original SP code never existed or cannot be found elsewhere.

bigpulp_tree.result: Hardware repository and pointer-chasing testbench paths; no original SP application entry identified.

official_relationship.evidence: Repository belongs to pulp-platform; copyright names ETH Zurich and University of Bologna. File history contains Andreas Kurth, a coauthor of arXiv1808.09751.

source_provenance.license: Apache-2.0; source file header lines 4–16; full license retained in hero/openmp-examples/LICENSE. Root LICENSE defines file-header precedence.

fixed_source_parameters.selection: Original no-argument default, unchanged: width=height=256. Do not choose a size to make a proposed scheduling rule favorable.
fixed_source_parameters.type: uint32_t input, accumulator and output; C=A*B^T with modulo-2^32 unsigned arithmetic.
fixed_source_parameters.allowed_source_argument_rule: Height argv is clamped to [32,512], stripe_height starts as height/2 and halves while stripe_height*height*4 >= 32KiB; height then truncates to n_stripes*stripe_height. Fixed evidence uses only original default256.
fixed_source_parameters.input_initialization: a[i*256+j]=i*256+j; b[i*256+j]=(i==j ? 2 : 0). Therefore expected c[i,j]=2*a[i,j] for default data.
fixed_source_parameters.data_dependent_optimization_boundary: Although default b is diagonal, the actual source runs the entire 256-term inner loop for every output. A compiler/algorithmic diagonal shortcut is a different kernel/work contract and must not silently replace it.

kernel_work.tile_indices: s=0..15 output row stripe, t=0..15 output column stripe
kernel_work.parallel_resources: One OpenMP team with num_threads(8), all participating in omp for collapse(2). Thread0 manages A, thread1 B, thread2 C. This is not an 8-cycle or 8-times-speed guarantee.
kernel_work.compute_timing: UNKNOWN on the current CVA6/iDMA platform. Optional upstream TIME_DMA_AND_COMP exists but is commented; no measured values have been retrieved or produced.

buffer_address_alias_contract.additional_costs: Six allocation records/pointers, six per-thread local job arrays, a_idx/b_idx/c_idx shared state, 8-thread OpenMP stacks/barriers/runtime, synchronization, descriptor supply and platform memory/cache support are additional. iDMA private copy buffer is not an application scratchpad slot.
buffer_address_alias_contract.host_alias: a,b,c,d are separate malloc allocations; function arguments a,b,c are __restrict__. C writes do not overlap A/B inputs. This differs from original SP one shared host input/output buffer.
buffer_address_alias_contract.halo: No halo or cross-stripe stencil. A/C external stripe stride equals stripe_bytes and stripes partition each array. B stripes likewise partition B but are replayed for each A stripe.

block_stride.B_source_byte_offset: t*16384 for each s; wraps to zero for next s

buffer_address_alias_contract.local_slots: A slot=s mod2; C slot=s mod2; B slot=(s*n_stripes+t) mod2 (for fixed n=16, equals t mod2). Slot generations must carry stream and source stripe, not merely slot parity.
buffer_address_alias_contract.compute_footprint: K(s,t) reads all A_s[0..4095] and all B_t[0..4095], writes C_s rows i=0..15 at columns t*16..t*16+15. Across all t it fills all C_s values.

notation.B_q: input B stripe q=(s,t), linear q=s*16+t
notation.D_s: output complete C row stripe s

source_event_contract.fill: Thread0 issues A0, thread1 B(0,0). At first outer/inner iterations they issue the next A/B into alternate slots before waiting for current input; barrier208 admits compute.
source_event_contract.input_A_lifetime: A_s slot is read by every K(s,t), t0..15; conservative release is end of K(s,15) including implicit omp-for completion barrier. A_(s+2) cannot overwrite until that release.
source_event_contract.input_B_lifetime: B(s,t) slot is read by K(s,t); release at implicit end-of-omp-for barrier. B at linear q+2 may overwrite afterward. At final t of each nonfinal s the next row first B stripe is prefetched (lines184–192).
source_event_contract.compute_ready: K(s,t) requires real completion of A_s and B(s,t), previous K completion, and D_(s-2) completion before reusing C_s slot for t0. Barrier208 synchronizes the three supply threads and team. Each omp for has an implicit completion barrier.
source_event_contract.output_lifetime: C_s contains incomplete output until all t complete. D_s is issued at beginning of s+1 by thread2. It waits previous D_(s-1) before current row reuse (source expression s>1 waits c_dma[c_idx]); C_s releases only when its own D_s is complete.
source_event_contract.drain: After last compute row, thread2 explicitly waits second-last D14, then issues blocking last D15. Parallel-region completion precedes free of all slots.
partial_order: application_complete>=done(D15) and all prior D completion
source_event_contract.source_completion_boundary: Upstream hero_dma_wait polls hardware completed transfer ID, separated from the issue ID. Header additionally requires calling wait exactly once per async transfer. For a CVA6/iDMA adaptation, issue, completion, data visibility and every B response must be tied to its actual platform contract; source reading here does not certify upstream AXI B retirement.
source_event_contract.async_setup_is_not_free: API permits asynchronous calls to block when hardware queues are full and does not guarantee constant issue cycles. Actual descriptor issue cost must be observed.

evidence.source_excerpt:
/** Asynchronous memcpy from host to device (`host2dev`) or from device to host (`dev2host`).

  These functions make a "best effort" to start the requested memcpy and then immediately return to
  the caller, so that the memcpy is executed in the "background" while the thread executes other
  code.  However, this is not always possible (e.g., when HW queues are full).  Thus, these
  functions may block for an undefined (but limited) number of cycles.  In short, these functions:
  - guarantee that the memcpy transfer has been started when they return;
  - do not guarantee to always return after a fixed number of cycles.

  On PULP, this is implemented using the DMA engine to or from cluster-internal L1 scratchpad memory
  from or to cluster-external memory.

  On the host, this is implemented with a call to `memcpy` and blocks until the entire memcpy has
  completed.

  \param   dst  The destination address to which the data shall be copied.
  \param   src  The source address from which the data shall be copied.
  \param   size The amount of data that shall be copied in bytes.

  \return  DMA job, which MUST be used to call hero_dma_wait to wait for the completion of this
           transfer before data is used.  Not calling the wait function exactly once per transfer
           initiated with these functions can entail undefined behavior.
 */
hero_dma_job_t hero_memcpy_host2dev_async(DEVICE_VOID_PTR dst,
                                          const HOST_VOID_PTR src,
                                          uint32_t size);
hero_dma_job_t hero_memcpy_dev2host_async(HOST_VOID_PTR dst,
                                          const DEVICE_VOID_PTR src,
                                          uint32_t size);

/** Wait for a previously issued non-blocking memcpy to finish.

  \param   job  The DMA job obtained from a previous call to hero_memcpy_*_async().
 */
void hero_dma_wait(hero_dma_job_t job);

fixed_transfer_budget.DMA_API_waits: A16+B256+C15 async waits plus the final blocking C copy (which itself waits once in PULP implementation).
fixed_transfer_budget.source_threads: Three software request streams mapped to a shared PULP multi-stream DMA interface. libhero-target defines DMA_MAX_NUM_STREAMS8; this is not evidence of 8 backend jobs always in flight or of the current iDMA budget.
fixed_transfer_budget.budget_adaptation_warning: A single victim iDMA serializes its own transfer path and differs from the upstream three-stream API. Two victim iDMAs still cannot be silently equated to three streams. State resource choice and include descriptor, compute and shared service costs.
fixed_transfer_budget.legal_simple_comparator: Permit ordinary retention/reuse of B stripes or cache when the same total on-chip/storage budget and code semantics allow it; do not force repeated B misses to create a new-rule gain.

mapping_and_portability_limits.meaning: At this pinned revision the active example uses target device1 copy-based offload. The SVM device0 path is wrapped in if(0) and documented as nonfunctional. Thus it supplies a real kernel/slot contract, not a ready-to-run upstream shared-IOMMU/SVM experiment.
mapping_and_portability_limits.adaptation_required: Choose real or modeled six-slot scratchpad, fixed compute implementation, actual DMA budgets, source/destination permissions and page lifetimes, cache/coherence/sync, and full stream drain; then generate events from that fixed executable. No current hardware ABI/RTL change is authorized by these findings.

minimal_functional_run_proposal.scope: Extract the unchanged host-reference multiply loop and original default input initialization to a host-only functional harness, with default256 and an exact checksum/output check c=2a. No hero DMA API or target offload calls. This demonstrates the actual fixed computation but not DMA overlap or slot lifetimes.
minimal_functional_run_proposal.why_not_original_full_host_binary: The upstream host implementations of asynchronous transfers are blocking memcpy and wait is no-op; its actual hero_l1malloc returns NULL despite the header comment claiming malloc. The complete upstream double_buf_mm therefore cannot run through its stock host fallback without a clearly labeled allocation/transfer adaptation.
minimal_functional_run_proposal.subsequent_event_goal: After root acceptance, port the real double_buf_mm loop structure with explicit A/B/C slot generations into a private host functional scheduler/trace adapter, retaining default parameters and arithmetic, comparing all outputs against original reference. Host memcpy events are logical CPU copy events, not hardware DMA done; current-platform DMA trace remains a later separate experiment.

all65536 outputs match expected2a and independently original host reference
exact source workload16,777,216 uint32 multiply-add steps
six16KiBslots and A16+B256+C16 transfer conservation if the adapter is created
